transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, um, I guess I'm here because things have been... really hard lately. Especially at the salon. It's like my hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. Even just sectioning hair or mixing color, it takes me forever now. People have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be. My manager actually pulled me aside the other day. She was wearing this bright pink scarf, and it reminded me of this scarf my aunt used to wear when I was a kid. We used to go to the beach every summer, and she would tie it around her hair so it wouldn't get frizzy. I loved the beach. The sand always felt so nice between my toes, and we'd collect seashells for hours... but yeah, I just can't seem to move as fast as I used to.
Besides feeling slower, have you noticed any shaking, stiffness, or trouble with your balance or walking?

Um, no, not really. No shaking or stiffness, and my balance is totally fine. I mean, my feet ache sometimes because I stand all day at the salon, but walking is okay. I actually just bought these new shoes for work because of that. They have this really thick memory foam in them. I got them at the mall last weekend. The mall was so crowded, though. There was this huge group of teenagers blocking the escalator, and they were all holding those massive iced coffees from the food court. I used to drink so much iced coffee when I was getting my associate's degree, like, three or four cups a day just to get through my morning classes. My favorite was the caramel macchiato, but they always put way too much ice in it, you know? But, um... yeah, no shaking or anything like that.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat sadness in my chest. It just sits there, like there's no point in trying to build the life I was planning, you know? I wanted to open my own salon by the time I was twenty-five. I even had a name picked out—Shear Magic. My friend Sarah thought it was a little cheesy, but she doesn't know anything about branding. She's going to school for accounting, which just sounds so boring to me. Staring at numbers all day... I could never do that. I need to be creative, working with colors and shapes. But lately, even mixing the hair dye just feels like a chore, and that sadness is just... always there.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or felt that people were watching you or trying to harm you?

Um, well, yeah, actually... sometimes when I'm sweeping up hair at the end of the day or rinsing out the color bowls in the back, I hear this woman's voice. She's usually over near the shampoo stations, and she just keeps saying that I'm ruining everything. But the thing is, the salon will be totally empty, or there's absolutely nobody near me. The shampoo stations are right next to the breakroom, and our breakroom is so tiny. We barely have room for the microwave, and someone keeps burning popcorn in it. The smell just lingers in the back hallway for days, and it mixes with the smell of the bleach and developers. It's honestly nauseating. My coworker, Jessica, always brings these huge Tupperware containers of leftover fish, and I've told her a million times you can't heat up fish in a small space like that, but she never listens. She thinks she runs the place just because she's been there for five years. But, um, yeah... I hear that voice telling me I'm ruining things when no one is there.
Does that voice only happen when you're feeling really down and heavy like you described, or do you also hear it at times when your mood feels normal?

Um, no, it's not just when I'm feeling down. Like, before the depression really took over and got so heavy, there was a stretch of several weeks where I was actually getting up and functioning pretty normally. But I was already hearing that woman's voice then, and I was also totally sure that someone at the salon was messing with my schedule on purpose. I'd look at the appointment book and things just seemed wrong. We use this digital booking system now, and it's supposed to make things easier, but honestly, the tablet they gave us is so old. The screen is cracked right down the middle because Jessica dropped it last month. She didn't even tell the manager, she just left it on the reception desk like nothing happened. And the WiFi in the salon is terrible, too. It always cuts out right when I'm trying to check a client out, and then they just stand there awkwardly while the little circle spins on the screen. It's so embarrassing. One lady actually got mad and left without tipping because it took so long. I usually rely on tips to pay for my gas, and gas prices have been ridiculous lately. I had to fill up my tank yesterday and it was almost fifty dollars. But, um... yeah, I was hearing the voice and feeling like someone was messing with my schedule even before I started feeling so sad.
Can you tell me roughly how many weeks or months you were hearing that voice and feeling like your schedule was being tampered with before the heavy sadness started?

Um, well, the voice and the feeling that someone was targeting my bookings... that's been going on for a while. Like, about a year and four months, I'd say. It started right around the time we got the new salon chairs. We used to have these awful, squeaky black ones that would get stuck when you tried to pump them up, and my back was always killing me. I actually had to go to a chiropractor for a few weeks because my lower back was just in knots. He told me I needed to stretch more and drink more water, which, I mean, everyone says that, right? Drink more water. I bought one of those big water bottles with the time markers on the side to try and keep track, but I always forget it in my car. And when it sits in the hot car all day, the water tastes like plastic. It's so gross. I tried putting lemon in it once to make it taste better, but the lemon just got all mushy. Anyway, yeah, it's been about a year and four months of the voice and the schedule stuff before the depression really hit.

During that year and four months before the heavy sadness began, were there any stretches where you had no depression at all—no low mood, no loss of interest—while you were still hearing that voice and feeling your schedule was being tampered with?

Yeah, like I think I mentioned a minute ago, there was definitely a stretch of several weeks right before the depression really took over where I wasn't sad at all. I was getting up, functioning completely normally, no low mood or anything. But I was already hearing that woman's voice and feeling totally sure someone at the salon was interfering with my schedule. I was actually getting to work early during those weeks, feeling pretty good. I'd stop at this little drive-thru coffee stand on the corner of Maple and 5th. They make these amazing iced oat milk lattes, but they recently changed their oat milk brand and it just doesn't foam the same way anymore. It's way too watery. I even asked the barista about it—her name is Chloe, she has this really cool split-dyed hair, half black and half neon green. I actually gave her my card for the salon because whoever did her green didn't lift it enough first, so it's looking a little muddy at the roots. You really have to bleach it to a pale yellow, like inside-of-a-banana color, before you put neon over it, otherwise it just looks swampy. I told her I could fix it for her, but I don't think she ever called to book. Which is fine, but it just bothers me when people walk around with bad color when it's such an easy fix. But um, anyway, what were we saying? Oh, right, yeah... there were definitely weeks where my mood was totally fine and normal, but the voice and the schedule stuff were still happening.

Since that period of several weeks when your mood was normal, has there ever been a stretch of at least two months where you were completely free of the voice and the feeling that your schedule was being tampered with?

Two months? Um, no, definitely not. It hasn't stopped for that long. It's pretty much just always there. Two months is actually a really long time... that's usually exactly how far out my regular clients book their root touch-ups. Like Mrs. Higgins, she comes in exactly every eight weeks, always on a Tuesday morning. She always brings these little blueberry muffins from the bakery next to her house. They're so good, but they have those giant, chunky sugar crystals baked on top, and last time I bit into one, I swear I almost chipped my front tooth. Dental work is so insanely expensive right now. My friend Sarah had to get a crown last month and it cost her like a thousand dollars out of pocket because her insurance wouldn't cover the porcelain one, only the metal one. And like, who wants a shiny silver tooth right near the front of their mouth? She was so upset about it. She actually called me crying from her car for like an hour. But um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the voice. No, I haven't had a two-month break from it or the schedule stuff at all.

But um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the voice. No, I haven't had a two-month break from it or the schedule stuff at all.

inference.note: The absence of any 2-month symptom-free interval, combined with clear psychotic symptoms (voice, delusional belief about schedule tampering) persisting for weeks without mood symptoms, and a later superimposed major depressive episode, fits schizoaffective disorder better than schizophrenia alone, which would require mood symptoms to be brief/incidental relative to the psychotic illness. This effectively rules out F20.9.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports continuous psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of a derogatory voice and persecutory delusions about schedule tampering) persisting for approximately 16 months without a 2-month symptom-free interval. Critically, there was a distinct period of several weeks where these psychotic symptoms occurred in the complete absence of any mood disturbance, establishing that psychosis is not solely a function of mood episodes. Subsequently, a major depressive episode (anhedonia, depressed mood, psychomotor slowing, hopelessness) emerged and is now co-occurring with the ongoing psychotic symptoms. This pattern—psychotic symptoms present both during and independent of a mood episode, with the mood episode present for a substantial portion of the total illness duration—meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type, rather than primary psychotic disorder (which would require mood episodes to be brief/absent) or MDD with psychotic features (which would require psychosis only during mood episodes).
